name: Pyramid setup: knight jumps to e5 when ...e5 is coming
moves: d4 d5 Bf4 Nf6 e3 e6 Nf3 Bd6 Bg3 O-O Bd3 Nc6 c3 Qe7 Ne5
videoTitle: Learn the London System | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Answer the bishop-trade offer by dropping back to g3, so a capture opens the h-file for White's rook. Once Black lines up ...e5, the knight lands on e5 itself, backed by the d4 pawn and the bishop, and f4 plus a queen swing follow.

name: Early ...Qb6: the knight to c3 makes the b2 pawn poison
moves: d4 d5 Bf4 c5 e3 Qb6 Nc3 Qxb2 Nb5
videoTitle: Learn the London System | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Against an early queen raid on b2, Nc3 offers the pawn: after the capture the knight jumps to b5 aiming at c7, where it forks king and rook, and the queen on b2 starts running out of squares.

name: Early ...Bf5: switch to a Queen's Gambit and hit b7
moves: d4 d5 Bf4 Bf5 c4 e6 Nc3 c6 Qb3
videoTitle: Learn the London System | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: When Black develops the light-squared bishop early, b7 loses its guard. White abandons the pyramid, plays c4 and Nc3, and brings the queen to b3 to press on b7.

name: Vs ...g6 and ...d5: the h4-h5 rook sacrifice idea
moves: d4 Nf6 Bf4 g6 Nc3 d5 e3 Bg7 h4 O-O h5 Nxh5 Rxh5 gxh5 Qxh5
videoTitle: Learn the London System | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: With Black's king castled into the fianchetto, the h-pawn marches to h5 and White gives up the rook on h5 to rip open the h-file; the queen then follows down it toward h7.

name: Vs ...g6 and ...d5: Black stops h5, White develops for a long castle
moves: d4 Nf6 Bf4 g6 Nc3 d5 e3 Bg7 h4 h5 Nf3 O-O Ne5
videoTitle: Learn the London System | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: If Black blocks the h-pawn with ...h5, White develops normally, puts a knight on e5, and prepares to castle queenside before storming the kingside.

name: Vs early ...c5 with the knight on f6: push d5, then the Vaganian gambit
moves: d4 Nf6 Bf4 c5 d5 Qb6 Nc3 Qxb2 Bd2
videoTitle: Learn the London System | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Against ...c5 White gains space with d5. If the queen grabs b2, the bishop retreats to d2 and White uses the tempi for e4 and f4, rolling the center while the black queen wanders.

name: Vs early ...c5 and ...d6: big center and long castle
moves: d4 Nf6 Bf4 c5 d5 d6 Nc3 e5 e4 exf4 Qd2
videoTitle: Learn the London System | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: When Black plays quietly after d5, White builds e4 behind the space pawn, brings the queen to d2 and castles long for a kingside pawn storm.

name: Taking on c5: the Bxb8 and Bb5+ trick against ...b6
moves: d4 d5 Bf4 Nf6 e3 c5 dxc5 e6 b4 b6 Bxb8 Rxb8 Bb5+ Bd7 c6
videoTitle: How to WIN with the London System!
idea: Grabbing on c5 and holding the pawn with b4 is a real option. If Black undermines with ...b6, removing the knight on b8 and checking on b5 lets the c-pawn charge forward with a discovered attack in reserve.

name: Vs ...c5 and ...Qb6: offer the queen trade on b3
moves: d4 d5 Bf4 Nf6 e3 c5 c3 Nc6 Nd2 Qb6 Qb3
videoTitle: How to WIN with the London System!
idea: Meet the queen raid by offering a trade on b3. White wants Black to capture, so White's a-file rook opens; taking first would open Black's rook instead.

name: Vs ...Qb6 trade offer: if ...c4, slide back and break with e4
moves: d4 d5 Bf4 Nf6 e3 c5 c3 Nc6 Nd2 Qb6 Qb3 c4 Qc2 g6 e4
videoTitle: How to WIN with the London System!
idea: If Black avoids the trade with ...c4, the queen steps back to c2 and Black's center is overextended, which makes the e4 break strong.

name: Why Nd2 comes before Nf3: the ...Bf5 shot on a trapped rook
moves: d4 d5 Bf4 Nf6 e3 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 Qb3 c4 Qc2 Bf5
videoTitle: How to WIN with the London System!
idea: With the knight already on f3 and b1 still blocked, the bishop on f5 cannot be taken: ...Qxb2 would win the cornered a1 rook. Developing the queen's knight to d2 first is what makes the trade-offer plan safe.

name: Vs ...Bd6: drop back to g3 rather than trade
moves: d4 d5 Bf4 Nf6 e3 e6 Nf3 Bd6 Bg3 O-O Bd3
videoTitle: How to WIN with the London System!
idea: Never capture on d6, since that hands Black control of e5. Retreat the bishop to g3 so that a trade on g3 straightens White's pawns toward the h-file.

name: Vs ...Bd6: let Black double the f-pawns
moves: d4 d5 Bf4 Nf6 e3 e6 Nf3 Bd6 Nbd2 Bxf4 exf4
videoTitle: How to WIN with the London System!
idea: An advanced option is to allow the trade on f4. The doubled pawns look ugly, but White gets a firm grip on e5 and an open e-file for a rook later.

name: Vs the King's Indian with ...d5: Nc3, Qd2 and Bh6
moves: d4 Nf6 Bf4 g6 Nc3 d5 Qd2 Bg7 Bh6
videoTitle: How to WIN with the London System!
idea: Against a fianchetto, Nc3 and Qd2 prepare to trade off the dark-squared bishop with Bh6. If Black castles kingside anyway, h4-h5 and a long castle follow.

name: Main line vs ...c5: rerouting the knight to e5 when ...Re8 prepares ...e5
moves: d4 d5 Bf4 Nf6 e3 e6 Nf3 c5 c3 Nc6 Nbd2 Bd6 Bg3 O-O Bd3 b6 Qe2 Re8 Ne5 cxd4 exd4
videoTitle: How to WIN with the London System!
idea: Black's ...Re8 is aimed at the ...e5 break, so White plants the knight on e5 first. When Black trades on d4, recapture with the e-pawn to open the e-file rather than with the c-pawn.

name: Vs ...c5 and ...Qb6: Nc3 and Nb5, where ...Na6 runs into a3
moves: d4 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3 Qb6 Nc3 Qxb2 Nb5 Na6 a3
videoTitle: Beat Agadmator's Anti-London System
idea: After the pawn grab and Nb5, guarding c7 with the knight from a6 does not save the queen: a3 cuts off its escape, and Rb1 plus a later Bc4 can box it in completely.

name: Vs ...c5 and ...Qb6: the main line after ...Nd5
moves: d4 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3 Qb6 Nc3 Qxb2 Nb5 Nd5 a3 a6 Rb1 Qa2 Qc1
videoTitle: Beat Agadmator's Anti-London System
idea: The knight to d5 is Black's only good defense. White can force a repetition or play a3, Rb1 and Qc1, which leaves the black queen short of squares in a messy fight.

name: Vs ...Qb6 and ...a6: the g4 pawn sacrifice
moves: d4 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3 Qb6 Nc3 a6 g4
videoTitle: Beat Agadmator's Anti-London System
idea: When ...a6 takes away b5, White throws in g4 to deflect the f6 knight and gain central space. Grabbing on g4 with the knight walks into Nd5.

name: Vs ...Qb6: Na3, and ...a6 meets Nc4 with a queen trap
moves: d4 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3 Qb6 Na3 a6 Nc4 Qb4+ c3 Qb5 Nd6+
videoTitle: Beat Agadmator's Anti-London System
idea: Na3 asks the queen a question. After ...a6, the knight hops to c4; a check on b4 is answered by c3, and when the queen steps to b5 the knight lands on d6 with check while the f1 bishop now hits the queen.

name: Vs ...Qb6, Na3 ...a6 Nc4: the only safe retreat is ...Qa7
moves: d4 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3 Qb6 Na3 a6 Nc4 Qa7
videoTitle: Beat Agadmator's Anti-London System
idea: Every other queen move gets punished, so Black must tuck the queen on a7; White then continues developing with gain of time against the misplaced queen.

name: Vs ...c5: d5 then Bd2 and a queenside clamp
moves: d4 Nf6 Bf4 c5 d5 d6 Nc3 e5 Bd2 Be7 e4
videoTitle: Beat Agadmator's Anti-London System
idea: Against a Benoni-style ...e5 the bishop drops to d2, White takes the center with e4 and clamps the queenside with a4 before considering a kingside pawn storm.

name: Taking on c5: ...Qa5+ is met by offering queens on d2
moves: d4 Nf6 Bf4 c5 dxc5 Qa5+ Qd2 Qxc5 Nc3 Nc6 e4
videoTitle: Beat Agadmator's Anti-London System
idea: After the check, Qd2 asks Black to either trade queens and stay a pawn down or retreat; then White develops with Nc3 and e4, aiming for a long castle and a pawn storm.

name: Taking on c5: vs ...Na6 the surprising f3
moves: d4 Nf6 Bf4 c5 dxc5 Na6 f3 Nxc5 e4
videoTitle: Beat Agadmator's Anti-London System
idea: Instead of defending the pawn, White plays f3 and e4 to build a big center; the same structure supports a later Bh6 and a kingside pawn storm.

name: Vs ...d5: take on f6 and build on dark squares with g3
moves: d4 Nf6 Bg5 d5 Bxf6 exf6 e3 Bd6 g3 O-O Bg2
videoTitle: CRUSH People With The Trompowsky Attack!
idea: Capturing on f6 damages Black's pawn structure. With the dark bishop gone, White keeps pawns on dark squares, fianchettoes the light bishop and expands on the queenside.

name: Vs ...d5: Stonewall structure with Nd2, Bd3, c3 and f4
moves: d4 Nf6 Bg5 d5 e3 e6 Nd2 Be7 Bd3 c5 c3 Nbd7 f4
videoTitle: CRUSH People With The Trompowsky Attack!
idea: Holding the g1 knight back lets White play f4 for a Stonewall grip on e5; unlike a normal Stonewall, the dark bishop is already outside the pawn chain and helps the kingside attack.

name: Vs ...d5 and ...Bf5: trade on f6 and switch to c4
moves: d4 Nf6 Bg5 d5 e3 Bf5 Bxf6 exf6 c4
videoTitle: CRUSH People With The Trompowsky Attack!
idea: When Black's light bishop comes to f5, White removes the f6 knight and changes plan to a quick c4, hitting the d5 pawn while b7 lacks support.

name: Vs ...c5: wedge with d5 and build a c4-f3-e4 wall
moves: d4 Nf6 Bg5 c5 d5 Ne4 f3 Nxg5 e4
videoTitle: CRUSH People With The Trompowsky Attack!
idea: Black's ...c5 is answered with d5, followed by a pawn wall in the center that leaves Black short of space.

name: Vs ...e6: the Big Center with e4
moves: d4 Nf6 Bg5 e6 e4 h6 Bxf6 Qxf6 Nc3 c5 Nf3
videoTitle: CRUSH People With The Trompowsky Attack!
idea: Against a Nimzo-minded ...e6, White takes the knight and claims two central pawns; with Black's queen exposed on f6, White develops quickly and keeps d5 in reserve.

name: Raptor: ...Ne4 h4, and ...d5 runs into g6
moves: d4 Nf6 Bg5 Ne4 h4 Nxg5 hxg5 d5 g6
videoTitle: CRUSH People With The Trompowsky Attack!
idea: If Black takes on g5, the h-file opens for White's rook. After ...d5 the pawn jumps to g6, and taking it with the h-pawn drops the h8 rook to the open file.

name: Raptor: after g6 fxg6, aim at the weakened g6 pawn
moves: d4 Nf6 Bg5 Ne4 h4 Nxg5 hxg5 d5 g6 fxg6 e3 Bf5 Bd3
videoTitle: CRUSH People With The Trompowsky Attack!
idea: If Black takes on g6 with the f-pawn, the kingside is a mess: White develops the bishop to d3 to hit g6, with tactics along the h-file against the rook.

name: Vs ...Ne4: Bf4, then take the knight and target the e4 pawn
moves: d4 Nf6 Bg5 Ne4 Bf4 d5 e3 c5 Bd3 cxd4 Bxe4 dxe4
videoTitle: CRUSH People With The Trompowsky Attack!
idea: With the bishop back on f4, White can trade on e4 so the pawn there becomes a fixed target; checks with the queen and a long castle add pressure.

name: Vs ...Ne4 and ...c5: d5 and the Bc1 retreat
moves: d4 Nf6 Bg5 Ne4 Bf4 c5 d5 Qb6 Bc1
videoTitle: CRUSH People With The Trompowsky Attack!
idea: When ...Qb6 eyes b2, the bishop can simply go home to c1; nothing is weakened, and White follows with f3 and e4 to evict the e4 knight and wedge the center.

name: Vs ...Ne4 and ...c5: f3, and ...Qa5+ is blocked with c3
moves: d4 Nf6 Bg5 Ne4 Bf4 c5 f3 Qa5+ c3 Nf6 d5
videoTitle: CRUSH People With The Trompowsky Attack!
idea: The f3 push kicks the knight; a queen check is blocked by c3, and then d5 grabs a lot of central space.

name: The perfect Stonewall: Bd3, Nd2, f4 and a knight on e5
moves: d4 d5 e3 Nf6 Bd3 e6 Nd2 Be7 f4 O-O Ngf3 Nc6 c3 a6 O-O b5 Ne5
videoTitle: Learn the Stonewall Defense & Attack | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Bd3 stops the light bishop reaching f5 and Nd2 keeps a black knight off e4; after f4 the knight sits on e5 supported by two pawns, and a rook lift via f3 to h3 joins the attack on h7.

name: Vs ...Nc6: play f4 at once to stop ...e5
moves: d4 d5 e3 Nf6 Bd3 Nc6 f4
videoTitle: Learn the Stonewall Defense & Attack | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Any black move that prepares ...e5 must be met by f4 immediately, otherwise the Stonewall never gets built.

name: Vs ...c5: support with c3 and recapture with the e-pawn
moves: d4 d5 e3 Nf6 Bd3 e6 Nd2 Be7 f4 c5 c3
videoTitle: Learn the Stonewall Defense & Attack | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: White answers ...c5 with c3, not a capture. If Black trades on d4, taking back with the e-pawn opens the e-file and keeps b4 covered.

name: Vs the King's Indian: no Nd2, aim for e4
moves: d4 Nf6 e3 g6 f4 Bg7 Nf3 O-O Bd3 d6 c3
videoTitle: Learn the Stonewall Defense & Attack | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Without a black pawn on d5 there is no ...Ne4 threat, so Nd2 is unnecessary; White reinforces with c3 and looks to push e4.

name: Catalan move order via Nf3 and a delayed c4
moves: d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6 g3 Bg7 Bg2 O-O O-O d6 c4
videoTitle: How to play the Catalan | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: White can go Nf3, g3, Bg2 and castle before pushing c4, aiming for the same Catalan structure while avoiding early commitments.

name: Vs ...c5: push d5 and support it with c4
moves: d4 c5 d5 e5 c4 d6 Nc3 Be7 e4
videoTitle: How to play the Catalan | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Against an early ...c5, gain space with d5, back it up with c4 and take the full center with e4.

name: Vs the Englund Gambit: keep the pawn, Nc3 and e4
moves: d4 e5 dxe5 Nc6 Nc3 Nxe5 e4
videoTitle: How to play the Catalan | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: No need for theory: take the pawn, develop the queen's knight, and if Black recaptures, take the center with e4 before developing the bishop and castling short.

name: Reverse Sicilian with g3: trade on d5 and develop
moves: c4 e5 g3 Nf6 Bg2 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 Nc3
videoTitle: How to play the English Opening | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Against ...e5 and ...d5 White trades on d5 and develops with gain of time against the centralized knight; b3 and Bb2 are a useful extra plan.

name: Reverse Sicilian with Nc3, e3 and Nge2, then a queenside expansion
moves: c4 e5 g3 Nc6 Bg2 g6 Nc3 Bc5 e3 Nf6 Nge2 O-O a3
videoTitle: How to play the English Opening | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: With the knight on e2 supporting the center, White expands on the queenside with a3, b4 and Rb1, complementing the long-diagonal bishop.

name: Flexible move order: 2.Nc3 and 3.e4 vs ...e6
moves: c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 e4
videoTitle: How to play the English Opening | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Answering ...e6 with e4 denies Black a Nimzo-Indian and claims the center immediately.

name: Vs a King's Indian setup: Be2, Be3 and a pawn storm before Nf3
moves: c4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 e4 d6 d4 Bg7 Be2 O-O Be3 e5 h4
videoTitle: How to play the English Opening | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Delaying Nf3 keeps the g- and h-pawns free: White plays h4 and h5 (and g4) with Qd2 and Bh6 to strip Black's king before even developing the knight.

name: Symmetrical English: Botvinnik setup with e4 and Nge2
moves: c4 c5 Nc3 Nc6 g3 g6 Bg2 Bg7 e4 d6 Nge2 e6 d3
videoTitle: How to play the English Opening | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: When Black copies, White builds the e4-d3 Botvinnik structure with the knight on e2; h3 before Be3 keeps the bishop from being hit.

name: Symmetrical English: the early h4 idea
moves: c4 c5 Nc3 Nc6 g3 g6 Bg2 Bg7 h4
videoTitle: How to play the English Opening | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Strong players sometimes push h4 early so the g1 knight can head to f4 via h3, adding kingside space in a symmetrical position.

name: Vs ...e6 and ...d5: Catalan-style gambit, regain with Qa4+
moves: c4 e6 g3 d5 Bg2 dxc4 Qa4+
videoTitle: How to play the English Opening | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: If Black grabs the c4 pawn, a queen check on a4 picks it back up, and the g2 bishop is left aiming down an open diagonal.

name: Vs ...c6 and ...d5: regain the pawn with Na3
moves: c4 c6 g3 d5 Bg2 dxc4 Na3
videoTitle: How to play the English Opening | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Against a Slav-style ...c6, White lets the pawn go and recovers it with the knight via a3 to c4.

name: Queen's Gambit Accepted: take the center, and ...b5 meets a4
moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e4 b5 a4 a6 axb5 axb5 Rxa8
videoTitle: How To Play The Queen's Gambit
idea: After the pawn grab, White claims two central pawns with e4. If Black holds c4 with ...b5, a4 undermines it, and recapturing with the a-pawn loses the a8 rook.

name: QGA with ...b5 and ...c6: the knight raid on b5
moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e4 b5 a4 c6 axb5 cxb5 Nc3 a6 Nxb5
videoTitle: How To Play The Queen's Gambit
idea: With ...c6 as support Black is still in trouble: after the trades on b5, Nc3 attacks the pawn again, and ...a6 fails because capturing back on b5 drops the rook on the a-file.

name: QGD with Bg5 and Qc2: the h4 'fishing pole' bait
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Be7 Bg5 O-O Qc2 h6 h4
videoTitle: How To Play The Queen's Gambit
idea: With the queen on c2 eyeing h7, h4 offers the g5 bishop: if ...hxg5, the h-file opens and the queen and rook crash through toward h7.

name: QGD with Bg5: the solid Bd3, castle and Rc1 plan
moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Be7 Bg5 O-O e3 h6 Bd3 hxg5 O-O g4 Rc1
videoTitle: How To Play The Queen's Gambit
idea: The steady approach: keep e3 until the bishop is out, develop to d3, castle, bring the rook to c1 and prepare e4.

name: Slav with an early ...Bf5: Qb3 hits b7
moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 Bf5 cxd5 cxd5 Qb3
videoTitle: How To Play The Queen's Gambit
idea: Once the light bishop leaves c8, b7 is loose; trading on d5 and bringing the queen to b3 hits b7 straight away.

name: Marshall Defense ...Nf6: take on d5 and grab the center
moves: d4 d5 c4 Nf6 cxd5 Nxd5 e4
videoTitle: How To Play The Queen's Gambit
idea: If Black defends d5 with the knight rather than a pawn, White captures and takes two central pawns with tempo on the knight.

name: Albin Countergambit: play Nf3 and fianchetto
moves: d4 d5 c4 e5 dxe5 d4 Nf3 Nc6 g3
videoTitle: How To Play The Queen's Gambit
idea: Against the Albin, avoid greed with e3; develop the king's knight and fianchetto, then work against the advanced d4 pawn.

name: Chigorin: stay solid with Nf3 and Nc3
moves: d4 d5 c4 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 Nc3
videoTitle: How To Play The Queen's Gambit
idea: Against the Chigorin, simple development is best: Nf3 and Nc3 keep d4 covered and leave Black's active pieces nothing to hit.

name: Baltic Defense: solid development with Nc3
moves: d4 d5 c4 Bf5 Nc3 e6 Nf3
videoTitle: How To Play The Queen's Gambit
idea: Against the early ...Bf5, stay compact and develop; the queenside will offer targets later.

name: Main line: f3, recapture with the knight, offer the bishop trade
moves: d4 d5 e4 dxe4 Nc3 Nf6 f3 exf3 Nxf3 Bf5 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3
videoTitle: FREE ELO With The Blackmar-Diemer Gambit
idea: White gives the e-pawn and then the f-pawn to open lines; after taking back on f3 with the knight, White develops fast, often castles long and uses the half-open f-file and a knight on e5.

name: If Black ignores f3 with ...e6, take back on e4
moves: d4 d5 e4 dxe4 Nc3 Nf6 f3 e6 fxe4
videoTitle: FREE ELO With The Blackmar-Diemer Gambit
idea: When Black declines to take on f3, White simply recaptures on e4 and is left with a big pawn center and easy development.

name: ...Bg4: h3, g4 and Ne5, then h4-h5 hunts the bishop
moves: d4 d5 e4 dxe4 Nc3 Nf6 f3 exf3 Nxf3 Bg4 h3 Bh5 g4 Bg6 Ne5 e6 h4
videoTitle: FREE ELO With The Blackmar-Diemer Gambit
idea: If the bishop pins the f3 knight, kick it with h3 and g4; once it drops to g6, the knight on e5 attacks it and the h-pawn threatens h5 to trap it.

name: Black's best: ...c5, answered by closing the center with d5
moves: d4 d5 e4 dxe4 Nc3 Nf6 f3 c5 d5
videoTitle: FREE ELO With The Blackmar-Diemer Gambit
idea: Black's strongest try strikes at d4 at once. Taking on c5 allows a queen trade, so White pushes d5, keeps the center closed and develops before cashing in.

name: Vs ...Bf5: Bg5 to undermine the f6 knight
moves: d4 d5 e4 dxe4 Nc3 Nf6 f3 Bf5 Bg5
videoTitle: FREE ELO With The Blackmar-Diemer Gambit
idea: Against the early ...Bf5, pressure on the f6 knight with Bg5 makes ...exf3 and the defense of e4 harder for Black; f3xe4 often follows.

name: Bg5 before f3
moves: d4 d5 e4 dxe4 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5
videoTitle: FREE ELO With The Blackmar-Diemer Gambit
idea: The bishop pin can come first, with f3 saved for later, so the f6 knight is pinned before the gambit pawn is offered.

name: Vs ...Nc6: push d5, and after ...Ne5 bring the queen to d4
moves: d4 d5 e4 dxe4 Nc3 Nf6 f3 Nc6 d5 Ne5 Qd4
videoTitle: FREE ELO With The Blackmar-Diemer Gambit
idea: Against ...Nc6 hitting d4, the pawn advances to d5. When the knight lands on e5, Qd4 attacks it, supports a later e5 push and keeps ...e6 off the board.

name: Reaching the gambit via 1...Nf6 2.Nc3
moves: d4 Nf6 Nc3 d5 e4 dxe4 f3
videoTitle: FREE ELO With The Blackmar-Diemer Gambit
idea: Against 1...Nf6, Nc3 prepares e4; if Black answers ...d5 and takes on e4, f3 transposes into the gambit.

name: 1...Nf6 2.Nc3 d5 3.e4 ...Nxe4: trade and aim at f7
moves: d4 Nf6 Nc3 d5 e4 Nxe4 Nxe4 dxe4 Bc4
videoTitle: FREE ELO With The Blackmar-Diemer Gambit
idea: If Black takes on e4 with the knight, trade on e4 and develop the bishop to c4, aiming at f7 with ideas of Qh5, Be3 and a long castle.

name: Nc3 and Bf4 against 1...Nf6
moves: d4 Nf6 Nc3 d5 Bf4
videoTitle: FREE ELO With The Blackmar-Diemer Gambit
idea: A system choice against 1...Nf6: the knight to c3 and bishop to f4 set up the Jobava London, ready to go Nb5 against c7.

name: Early Nc3 and Nb5 aiming at c7
moves: d4 d5 Bf4 c5 Nc3 Nc6 Nb5
videoTitle: How to WIN with the London System!
idea: With the c-pawn gone from c7, the knight jumps to b5 to land on c7 with the bishop's help, a forking idea in the style of a reversed Fried Liver.

name: Vs the Dutch: e4, Nc3 and Bg5
moves: d4 f5 e4 fxe4 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5
videoTitle: EVERY Chess Gambit for White and Black | Chess Opening Tips
idea: Against 1...f5, White gives a pawn with e4, develops the knight and pins on g5, aiming to remove the f6 knight and win back e4 with quick development.

name: Vs ...d5: Qh5+ wins back the d5 pawn
moves: d4 f5 e4 fxe4 Nc3 d5 Qh5+ g6 Qxd5 Qxd5 Nxd5
videoTitle: EVERY Chess Gambit for White and Black | Chess Opening Tips
idea: If Black holds e4 with ...d5, the queen check on h5 forces ...g6 and the queen picks off d5, leaving White a pawn back and a knight on d5.

name: Vs 1...Nf6: throw in g4 and take the center
moves: d4 Nf6 g4 Nxg4 e4
videoTitle: EVERY Chess Gambit for White and Black | Chess Opening Tips
idea: An aggressive anti-Indian idea: the g-pawn is offered to deflect the knight, and White grabs the center with e4 before developing the knights.

name: If Black ignores g4, kick the knight with g5
moves: d4 Nf6 g4 d5 g5
videoTitle: EVERY Chess Gambit for White and Black | Chess Opening Tips
idea: When Black declines the g-pawn, it advances to g5 to chase the f6 knight away from the center.

name: Vs the Dutch: the e4 gambit idea
moves: c4 f5 e4 fxe4 Nc3 Nf6 g4
videoTitle: EVERY Chess Gambit for White and Black | Chess Opening Tips
idea: Against an English-Dutch, White can strike with e4 and then g4-g5 to open Black's king position.

name: White vs the Englund: Nc3 refutes the ...Qe7 setup
moves: d4 e5 dxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Qe7 Nc3
videoTitle: EVERY Chess Gambit for White and Black | Chess Opening Tips
idea: Take the gambit pawn and, after ...Qe7, develop the queen's knight instead of Bf4; this keeps b4 covered and leaves White clearly better.

name: Open Catalan: Qc2 and a4 against ...a6
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 d5 g3 Be7 Bg2 O-O O-O dxc4 Qc2 a6 a4
videoTitle: 5 Most ANNOYING Chess Openings
idea: After Black finally takes on c4, the queen sets out to win the pawn back; when ...a6 prepares ...b5, a4 stops it and the g2 bishop keeps squeezing the queenside.

name: ...Bb4+ Catalan: block with Bd2 and trade dark bishops
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 d5 g3 Bb4+ Bd2
videoTitle: Magnus Carlsen Teaches The Catalan Opening
idea: When Black checks on b4, White blocks with the bishop and is happy to trade dark-squared bishops, keeping the g2 bishop as the long-term trump.

name: Closed Catalan with ...c6: Qc2 and play for e4
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 d5 g3 Be7 Bg2 O-O O-O c6 Qc2
videoTitle: Magnus Carlsen Teaches The Catalan Opening
idea: If Black keeps the center closed with ...c6, White brings the queen to c2 to support an eventual e4 and keeps pressure on the long diagonal.

name: Accepting the Benko: the king-walk main line
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5 cxb5 a6 bxa6 Bxa6 Nc3 d6 e4 Bxf1 Kxf1 g6 g3 Bg7 Kg2 O-O Nf3 Nbd7 a4
videoTitle: 5 Most ANNOYING Chess Openings
idea: White grabs the gambit pawns, trades the light bishops with e4 and walks the king to g2 instead of castling; a4 then fixes Black's queenside play.

name: Declining with e3: build Nc3, a4 and e4
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5 e3 bxc4 Nc3 d6 e4
videoTitle: 5 Most ANNOYING Chess Openings
idea: Instead of grabbing pawns, White guarantees regaining material and builds a crown of pawns with Nc3, e4 and a4, denying Black the usual open a- and b-files.

name: Declining with Qc2: if ...bxc4, take the center
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5 Qc2 bxc4 e4
videoTitle: 5 Most ANNOYING Chess Openings
idea: With the queen on c2, capturing on c4 opens no files for Black, and White recovers the pawn while taking the center with e4.

name: Modern Benoni: the four-pawns style with f4
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 e6 Nc3 exd5 cxd5 d6 e4 g6 f4
videoTitle: 5 Most ANNOYING Chess Openings
idea: Against the Benoni, White builds a big pawn center with e4 and f4, the same idea as the Four Pawns against the King's Indian.

name: Modern Benoni: Nf3 and an early Bf4
moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 e6 Nc3 exd5 cxd5 d6 Nf3 g6 Bf4
videoTitle: 5 Most ANNOYING Chess Openings
idea: A tricky alternative: develop the knight and put the bishop on f4 to pressure d6 before Black finishes the fianchetto setup.

name: Meran sideline with Be2
moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6 e3 Nbd7 Be2
videoTitle: 5 Most ANNOYING Chess Openings
idea: To avoid the main-line Meran, the bishop goes to e2 so a capture on c4 does not come with gain of time; a4 can then stop ...b5.

name: Quiet setup with b3, Bb2 and Qc2
moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6 e3 Nbd7 b3 Bb4 Bb2 Ne4 Qc2
videoTitle: 5 Most ANNOYING Chess Openings
idea: A solid way to sidestep the Meran: support c4 with b3, fianchetto the dark bishop and put the queen on c2 before castling.

name: Start with Nf3 to keep the English without allowing ...e5
moves: Nf3 d5 c4
videoTitle: STOP PLAYING These 4 Chess Openings
idea: Opening with the knight first stops ...e5, and White can still play c4 next, reaching English or Reti positions on better terms.

name: Nf3 ...Nc6: d4 and c4 for a favorable Chigorin
moves: Nf3 Nc6 d4 d5 c4
videoTitle: STOP PLAYING These 4 Chess Openings
idea: Many players answer Nf3 with ...Nc6; after d4 and c4 White has a version of the Chigorin that is pleasant for White.

name: Reversed Dragon trap: Nd5, Bg5 and a queen sacrifice mate
moves: c4 e5 Nc3 Nc6 Nf3 g6 d4 exd4 Nd5 Bg7 Bg5 Nge7 Nxd4 Bxd4 Qxd4 Nxd4 Nf6+ Kf8 Bh6#
videoTitle: 10 Chess Traps to Win FAST!!
idea: After ...exd4 the knight goes to d5 instead of recapturing. Bg5 forces a block on e7, and when the bishop takes on d4 White gives up the queen: the knight check on f6 and Bh6 mate follow.

name: Queen's Gambit Declined in eight moves: develop the bishop before e3
moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 Bf4 dxc4 e3 b5 Bd3 cxd3 O-O
videoTitle: The Queens Gambit
idea: If Black declines, develop both knights, bring the dark bishop out before playing e3 so it is not locked in, then develop the other bishop and castle.

name: Pyramid setup in 30 seconds: c3 against ...c5, knights to f3 and d2
moves: d4 d5 Bf4 Nf6 e3 e6 Nf3 c5 c3 Nc6 Nbd2 Bd6 Bd3 Bxf4 O-O
videoTitle: EASY Chess Opening
idea: Bishop to f4 before e3, knights to f3 and d2, and every time Black plays ...c5 answer with c3 to complete the pawn pyramid before castling.

name: 1.Nc3 d5 2.e4: a Caro-Kann structure without ...c6
moves: Nc3 d5 e4 dxe4 Nxe4
videoTitle: A Spicy Chess Opening — The "Dunst"
idea: After 1.Nc3 d5, e4 invites a trade; once the knight recaptures on e4 the position resembles a Caro-Kann in which Black has not played ...c6.

name: 1.Nc3 d5 2.e4 d4: reroute the knight via e2
moves: Nc3 d5 e4 d4 Nce2
videoTitle: A Spicy Chess Opening — The "Dunst"
idea: If Black gains space with ...d4, the knight steps back to e2 and heads for a better square such as g3.

name: Grob: Bg2 and c4 against ...Bxg4
moves: g4 d5 Bg2 Bxg4 c4
videoTitle: I Tried The Worst Chess Openings
idea: The Grob gives up the g-pawn to open the long diagonal; after ...Bxg4, c4 hits d5 and sets up tricks against b7. Even so, the engine considers it bad for White.

name: Marshall Defense with ...Qxd5: Nc3, Nf3 and e4
moves: d4 d5 c4 Nf6 cxd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd8 Nf3 e6 e4
videoTitle: How To Play The Queen's Gambit
idea: If Black recaptures on d5 with the queen, develop with tempo via Nc3, add Nf3, and then claim the center with e4.

name: Vs ...c5 and ...Qb6: the Vaganian gambit with Nc3 and Bd2
moves: d4 Nf6 Bg5 c5 d5 Qb6 Nc3 Qxb2 Bd2 Qb6 e4 d6 f4
videoTitle: CRUSH People With The Trompowsky Attack!
idea: White lets the b2 pawn go, retreats the bishop to d2 and, after the queen returns, overruns the center with e4 and f4.

name: Vs ...c5 and ...Qb6: the quiet Bc1 retreat
moves: d4 Nf6 Bg5 c5 d5 Qb6 Bc1 g6 f3 Bg7 e4
videoTitle: CRUSH People With The Trompowsky Attack!
idea: Rather than gambit b2, the bishop goes home to c1 where nothing can hit it; White then builds f3 and e4 to cramp Black.
